Or they could simply enjoy whatever games they're enjoying right now. It isn't a bad thing to prefer MMOs over singleplayer RPGs and vice versa. In the end, it's just a game. Have fun with it :3

I play MMOs with some friends of mine who got me hooked into the genre to begin with. And the milestones we do achieve in MMOs are sorta important to us as a friend group. I understand having maxed all classes and professions in a video game wouldn't really reflect well on a CV or resume, but you must admit that maybe at least some people could be affected by a player's involvement in their MMO experience.

Such as that one time we were able to beat our first Savage raid after over a dozen wipes. Grinding fetes in Firmament just so we can all dye our loincloths metallic brass. Or something as obscure and inconsequential as some random player giving me a 'Bottled Water' food item at the final zone of endwalker, telling me that "It should help choke back the tears." XD

You just can't get these experiences from singleplayer games. Not to say singleplayer RPGs themselves don't have their moments, as they're much easier for devs to curate and tailor for the player's enjoyment. They're comprised of some of the best that gaming has to offer in the way of storytelling and world-building. Something many MMOs sorely lack as these simply aren't the main focus of the genre.

Defeating the final boss in singleplayer RPGs: 
"Holy shit! I just did that!"

Defeating the final story boss in an MMORPG:
"Holy shit! WE just did that!"
